Jeleniewo Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Jeleniewo, Poland

Not demolished. Jeleniewo's Jewish community, likely settled from the mid-18th century, made up 37 percent of the village by 1921. In December 1939, the Germans deported the community to Suwałki and then Łomazy, with some also likely sent to Biała Podlaska; all or most of Jeleniewo's Jews were murdered during WWII. This cemetery, likely established in the second half of the 18th century, suffered extensive postwar damage, described in a 1989 survey as leaving tombstones and graves 'completely invisible.' In the early 1990s, at the initiative of Herman Storick of Larchmont, New York, the cemetery was cleaned, fenced with a stone wall, and given a monument designed by Cecilia Storick; a brochure on the history of Jeleniewo's Jews and a tombstone catalog were also published.
